A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TraMark research. All 13 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A.1–A.11, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original federated-learning experiments measuring task accuracy, watermark verification, robustness and scalability in Section 5 and Appendices A.6–A.10.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons, hyperparameter studies and appendix robustness evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same warmup, parameter-region selection, masked aggregation, watermark injection and verification procedures. The output-space extension in Appendix A.10 is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use FMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet, with MNIST, SVHN and WafflePattern watermark sources. The IID/non-IID, client-sampling, attack and label-space-extension scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FedAvg, WAFFLE and FedTracker as comparators. Comparator participation in the other reported experiments is also unchanged; no evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and the appendices retain the same model configurations, data partitioning, training budgets, MA/VR definitions, verification procedure, client-sampling settings and attack protocols.

E4.justification: The warmup, partition-ratio and watermark-size studies, output-divergence analysis, and pruning, fine-tuning, quantization and RNP robustness evaluations are retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report three repetitions with different seeds and averaged results in Section 5.1. Appendix A.7 retains the same t-tests and p-value threshold reporting in Table 4.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and reported findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 1 retains average MA values of 64.90% for TraMark and 65.44% for FedAvg. Appendix Tables 4–7 and Figures 1–6 also retain the same results.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–4, the constrained formulation in Problem 1, mathematical derivations and attack/defense assumptions are unchanged. Neither version supplies the theoretical traceability guarantee identified as future work in Appendix A.11.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: formalizing traceable black-box watermarking and proposing server-side TraMark to support traceability while preserving task performance. No core claim is strengthened or narrowed.

C2.justification: Interpretations of watermark collisions, robustness and scalability are unchanged. Appendices A.10–A.11 retain the same label-space limitation, collusion concern, computational-overhead discussion and lack of theoretical guarantees.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, the PyTorch implementation detail in Appendix A.3, hardware information in A.5, and code/data access information are unchanged. The added acknowledgment concerns funding and publication rights.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and positioning in Appendix A.2 and Table 3 are unchanged. References displaced onto page 9 in v3 are retained works, not new citations.

P1.justification: v3 adds an Acknowledgments section before References covering DOE funding, UT-Battelle and publication rights/public access. The arXiv version/date notice changes; scientific wording and section organization otherwise remain unchanged apart from minor spacing.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment reflows the reference list across pages 8–9, with small spacing and line-break changes elsewhere. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–7 retain their designs, content and page placements.

improvement.justification: v3 adds funding and publication-rights disclosure, improving administrative completeness. The scientific argument, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged, while presentation adjustments are small; there is no meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
